review_cost.rationale: Approve-able structure with one must-fix bug, one cache fix and a dead-code cleanup — a single round of concrete changes, not rework; everything else is nits.

findings.issue: Sortable column keys 'move' and 'type' don't exist on the row objects (which use moveName/moveDisplay/typeName/typeDisplay, views.mjs:427-436), so sorting by the Move or Type header hits the both-missing branch in sortRows (views.mjs:283-284), which ignores direction — the table silently stays in default order while the header gets aria-sort=ascending/descending (views.mjs:346).
findings.suggestion: Map column keys to row fields (e.g. key 'move' → moveDisplay, 'type' → typeDisplay), or rename row fields to match; add a guard that ignores unknown sortKey values so aria-sort can't lie.

findings.issue: versionGroupCache stores the raw promise and never evicts on rejection; one transient API failure permanently 500s that version group until restart (unlike memoize at api.mjs:134-145, which clears on error).
findings.suggestion: Reuse the rejection-clearing memoize pattern, or delete the cache entry when the promise rejects.

findings.issue: Dead exports renderMovePageByName/renderAbilityPageByName/renderTypePageByName (and unused typeDisplayName at api.mjs:192) duplicate the data orchestration that server.mjs:73-93 performs inline — two near-identical copies, one of which is never called.
findings.suggestion: Delete the dead helpers (or make the routes use them and delete the inline copies), so one canonical place assembles data per page.

findings.issue: Each sort click re-runs the entire page pipeline — getSpecies, default Pokémon, evolution chain, all move details and version groups (views.mjs:556-571) — to re-render a single table, relying entirely on the process cache to keep it cheap.
findings.suggestion: Either sort client-side for already-rendered tables, or cache the computed movesData keyed by species+game so the sort endpoint is a pure re-render.

findings.issue: Static assets are hand-served via boot-time readFileSync and c.body with hardcoded content types, instead of serveStatic from @hono/node-server/serve-static, and responses carry no Cache-Control so the ~50KB htmx bundle refetches on every page load.
findings.suggestion: Use serveStatic({ root: './public' }) and add Cache-Control headers for hashed/immutable assets.

findings.issue: onError logs the error but serves the 'Not found' page body with status 500, conflating server errors with 404s for both users and monitoring.
findings.suggestion: Render a distinct error page ('Something went wrong') for 500s.

findings.issue: fetchJson has no timeout or AbortController, so a hung upstream hangs requests indefinitely and can pile up the pending map.
findings.suggestion: Wrap fetch in AbortSignal.timeout(...) and treat timeouts as retriable errors.

findings.issue: The runtime cache is an unbounded Map with no TTL or eviction while the spec says to treat the API as a live service whose data can change at any moment (spec-allowed, but permanently stale once warm).
findings.suggestion: Add a simple TTL or a bounded LRU, and document the intended staleness window.

findings.issue: views.mjs is 624 lines mixing data assembly (getHomeData, getPokemonPageData, getMovesData) with rendering, and the whole codebase has zero comments (measured commentLines: 0) — the cache regime, HX-Target partial contract and sort-key mapping are all undocumented invariants.
findings.suggestion: Split data assembly from rendering, and add short comments on the non-obvious invariants (partial-response gating, cache behavior).

summary: A well-structured, current-idiom Hono + htmx app on pin-current dependency versions with genuinely careful htmx partial handling and request coalescing. Its one must-fix defect is that sorting by the Move or Type table header is a silent no-op that still sets aria-sort, caused by sort keys that don't match row field names. Merge after fixing that bug, the permanently-cached-rejection version-group cache, and deleting the duplicated dead route helpers — the rest is polish.
